proof_nl:
Fix an arbitrary positive integer d. Define
A := {i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}
and
B := {i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}.

We split the index set {1,...,b} into the disjoint union {1,...,a} union {a+1,...,b}. (If a=0 or a=b, one of these sets is empty, and the same argument still applies.) Therefore A is the disjoint union of A ∩ {1,...,a} and A ∩ {a+1,...,b}, and similarly for B.

For i with 1 <= i <= a, the definition gives e_i = i. Hence
|A ∩ {1,...,a}| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}|.

For i with a < i <= b, the definition gives e_i = r+i. The map i -> r+i is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} onto the set {m in Z : r+a < m <= r+b}. Under this bijection, the condition d divides e_i is exactly the condition d divides m. Thus
|A ∩ {a+1,...,b}| = |{m in Z : r+a < m <= r+b and d divides m}| = M_d(r+a,r+b).

Since the two pieces are disjoint,
|A| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}| + M_d(r+a,r+b).

Now do the same for B. Clearly,
|B ∩ {1,...,a}| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}|.
Also, the identity map is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} onto {m in Z : a < m <= b}, so
|B ∩ {a+1,...,b}| = |{m in Z : a < m <= b and d divides m}| = M_d(a,b).
Therefore,
|B| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}| + M_d(a,b).

By the hypothesis of the lemma, for this positive integer d we have
M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b).
Comparing the formulas for |A| and |B|, we obtain
|A| >= |B|,
that is,
|{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|.

Because d was arbitrary, this holds for every positive integer d, exactly as claimed.
solver_summary: Fix d>0 and split the indices into 1<=i<=a and a<i<=b. On the first part, e_i=i, so the two divisibility counts are identical. On the second part, i -> r+i is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} to the integer interval (r+a,r+b], so the count of indices with d dividing e_i is M_d(r+a,r+b), while the count of indices with d dividing i is M_d(a,b). The assumed inequality M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) then gives the desired conclusion.
vetter_reason: The proof is a complete direct counting argument. For fixed positive d, it partitions the index set {1,...,b} into {1,...,a} and {a+1,...,b}, uses the definition e_i=i on the first part and e_i=r+i on the second, and identifies the second-part count with M_d(r+a,r+b). Doing the same for divisibility of i identifies the comparison count with M_d(a,b). The assumed inequality then gives the desired result. The proof matches the lemma statement and assembly role, and it uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
